gap: No result ChatGPT got states a lab-measured brightness, colour or power figure for any candidate extender. No such measurement exists for these models. The closest named finding is Macworld's statement that the Trio 3 Pro's screens can't reach their 300-nit maximum on laptop power alone, and Dealectric's own cited pages already say that.
standout_why: Compared against: Macworld 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac' (cited), which lists the Trio 3 Pro's 300 nits, 100% sRGB, 72% NTSC and 4.13 lb with no sign that they were measured; Macworld's multi-monitor guide (cited), which has no extender and no measured figure, only general DisplayLink latency and CPU warnings; and Dealectric's best-triple-laptop-screen-extender page (cited), which already has Macworld's laptop-power brightness limit and CHIP.pl's 11 W draw. Every candidate review I opened (Macworld, CHIP.pl, Android.com.pl, Serious Insights) repeats the maker's specs. None measured anything, so this angle adds little that is new.
decides: It confirms the pick and doesn't change it. No named lab has measured brightness, colour or power for the Trio 3 Pro, Xebec Tri-Screen 3, UPERFECT Z 14, INVZI Trio Go 16 or KEFEYA S2Pro, so panel quality can't separate them. The pick should still rest on M1/M2/M3 driver support and fit on a 13-inch or 15-inch lid. The one usable named point is for Trio 3 Pro buyers: plan on the power adapter, because Macworld found the screens can't reach full brightness on laptop power, and CHIP.pl found them visibly dimmer than a MacBook's display.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power (Macworld, Simon Jary)
findings.value: Can't reach the 300-nit maximum on laptop power alone; full brightness needs the power adapter, which also passes up to 65 W to the laptop
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review | Macworld
findings.note: Review dated 2026-04-02, tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro (chip not given). Hands-on observation with no nit reading. The review doesn't say whether its spec figures (300 nits, 100% sRGB, 72% NTSC, 4.13 lb) were measured or taken from Mobile Pixels.

findings.label: Mac driver need (Macworld, Simon Jary)
findings.value: Base M1/M2 Macs need Mobile Pixels' free DisplayLink-like software for both screens; M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and any M4/M5 Mac work without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review | Macworld
findings.note: Quotes the manual: no driver is needed if the laptop has two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports. Jary calls the driver install fairly simple and one-time. A MacBook Air wasn't tested.

findings.label: Power draw and panel comparison (CHIP.pl, Kacper Cembrowski)
findings.value: 11 W in use (spec table); screens weaker than the MacBook Pro 14" display in brightness, contrast and black level
findings.source_title: Test Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro. Trzy ekrany w plecaku i MacBook pośrodku – CHIP.pl
findings.note: Published 2026-09-18. The 11 W figure is in CHIP's spec table and no instrument is named, so treat it as a spec, not a measurement. The brightness/contrast comparison is the reviewer's side-by-side judgement on a MacBook Pro 14". The same table gives 1.9 kg, 2240×1400 and 187 PPI.

findings.label: Weight, conflicting spec (Android.com.pl, Łukasz Pająk)
findings.value: 1.81 kg in its spec table, against 1.9 kg (4.13 lb) at Macworld and CHIP.pl
findings.source_title: Test Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro i Float 2 – Android.com.pl
findings.note: Published 2026-08-25. No scale named, so neither weight is a measurement. The reviewer says brightness is limited and may not be enough outdoors in strong sun, and that the full brightness may need extra power. No laptop model is named.

findings.label: Brightness and weight (Serious Insights, Daniel W. Rasmus)
findings.value: Rated up to 300 nits and 3.6 lb, both passed on from Xebec; the reviewer lists 300 nits as a limit in bright rooms and the weight as a caveat
findings.note: Review dated 2026-05-06. No test laptop named and nothing measured. It confirms that the Mac adapter uses DisplayLink chips and the free DisplayLink driver, with a Mac total of about $758.

unsourced: A lab-measured brightness (cd/m²), colour gamut or power draw for the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro. I checked Macworld, CHIP.pl, Android.com.pl, RTINGS, Notebookcheck, PCMag, Tom's Hardware and Tom's Guide; each review I opened gives maker specs only.

RTINGS' measured SDR brightness for the original Mobile Pixels TRIO (a different, older model). The review and comparison pages loaded only navigation text, and search snippets don't count as a source.
Any named measurement for the Xebec Tri-Screen 3. Serious Insights repeats Xebec's 300 nits and 3.6 lb, and I found no LaptopMag, Tom's Guide, ZDNet, RTINGS or Notebookcheck review.
Any named measurement for the UPERFECT Z 14 Tri Screen (BE14BF). The only review in the results, wetried.it's (not opened), describes a 1080p panel that doesn't match the 2240×1400 BE14BF.
Any review or measurement of the INVZI MagHub Trio Go 16 or the KEFEYA S2Pro 14". Searches returned only an unrelated KEFEYA S1 review.
A test of any of these extenders on a MacBook Air of any chip. Every named reviewer used a MacBook Pro 14" or didn't name the laptop.
